news.title: Andy Burnham says he wants to bring men’s World Cup back to UK in 2042
news.lede: PM tells regional mayors he is keen for tournament to be hosted in UK for first time since 1966. Andy Burnham has said he wants to bring the men’s World Cup to the UK in 2042, a move which would see the tournament return to these shores for the first time in almost eight decades. At a meeting in No 10 North in Manchester on Friday, the prime minister told regional mayors he was keen for the tournament to be played in the British Isles. When the 1966 World Cup took place in England, with the home side beating West Germany 4-2 in the final after extra time, it was the only time the country has either hosted or won the contest.

news.title: FIFA sanctions Argentina over brawl at World Cup final game
news.lede: Argentina’s defeat in the football World Cup final defeat has come with a costly post-match hangover. FIFA has imposed a ban on Argentine midfielder Leandro Paredes and a hefty fine for sparking a brawl after his side's loss to Spain. His teammate Nahuel Molina has been similarly disciplined in a series of a decisions by the FIFA disciplinary committee.

news.title: Argentina hit with sanctions for Falklands banner, World Cup final brawl
news.lede: Argentina have been hit with major sanctions by Fifa over their display of a Falkland Islands banner, while two players face lengthy bans for their actions in the World Cup final. After beating England 2-1 in their Fifa World Cup semi-final, Argentina players paraded a banner that read “Las Malvinas son Argentinas”, which translates to the Falklands belong to Argentina. Three EPL players, including Manchester United’s Lisandro Martinez and former Tottenham Hotspurs players Cristian Romero and Giovani Lo Celso, were pictured with the banner. The rivalry between the two nations over the islands was a hot topic before the match, with the tension being traced back to the South American nation’s invasion of the Falklands in 1982.
